newsitem.title: USA: Consumers sees 780 MW nuke back in a week.
newsitem.headline: Consumers sees 780 MW nuke back in a week.

text.p: Consumers Energy said Tuesday its 780 megawatt Palisades nuclear power station would resume operation in a week after it was shut Monday for repairs.
"The decision was made last night to take the unit off line. It'll be back on line in a week," a company spokesman said.

The restart of the generating station was interrupted when engineers discovered excessive leakage at a couple of main steam isolation valves. They also determined a primary coolant pump seal needed to be replaced.
The Palisades plant, which was originally shut Sunday for electrical repairs, returned on line briefly yesterday.
The South Haven, Mich., facility produces 18 percent of Consumer Energy's total electricity output.
Consumers Energy is a subsidiary of CMS Energy.
